classification: Integer-overflow-to-buffer-overflow (CWE-190/191/680) manifesting as an out-of-bounds write (CWE-787). ProtoTraceParser::ParsePowerRails uses a 32-bit, attacker-controlled power-rail index (desc.index(), uint32) with no upper bound both to size (resize) and to subscript the std::vector power_rails_strs_id_. For the PoC index UINT32_MAX (0xFFFFFFFF) the size computation idx + 1 overflows the 32-bit unsigned arithmetic and wraps to 0, so resize(idx + 1) becomes resize(0) and never grows the vector; the following store power_rails_strs_id_[idx] then subscripts an (empty) vector at index 0xFFFFFFFF and writes to a wild address.
bug_description: ProtoTraceParser::ParsePowerRails() iterates the rail_descriptor entries of an attacker-controlled PowerRails submessage and reads an index via desc.index() (uint32). It resizes power_rails_strs_id_ to idx+1 only when the current size is <= idx, then stores into power_rails_strs_id_[idx]. No upper bound is enforced on idx. The PoC supplies idx = 0xFFFFFFFF (UINT32_MAX, 4294967295). The size guard power_rails_strs_id_.size() <= idx is true (size 0 <= huge), so the resize branch is taken, but resize(idx + 1) evaluates idx + 1 in 32-bit unsigned arithmetic, which overflows and wraps to 0 (0xFFFFFFFF + 1 == 0); resize(0) leaves the vector empty. The subsequent store power_rails_strs_id_[idx] = InternString(counter_name) subscripts the empty vector at index 0xFFFFFFFF, writing far out of bounds and producing the ASan SEGV at proto_trace_parser.cc:863. The fix adds `if (PERFETTO_UNLIKELY(idx > 256)) continue;` to skip excessively large indices before the resize/subscript.

source.value_from: Untrusted trace bytes: the TracePacket.power_rails submessage supplied by the libFuzzer_perfetto_trace_processor_fuzzer input. The PowerRails::Decoder parses this attacker-controlled blob, and its repeated rail_descriptor field carries the RailDescriptor.index varint that becomes the out-of-bounds subscript.
source.note: Project-level materialization of the untrusted PowerRails submessage. The generic harness entry (LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput / FuzzTraceProcessor) is deliberately NOT used as the source; this Decoder construction is the first parse/load of the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.note: Out-of-bounds store: power_rails_strs_id_ (std::vector<StringId>) is subscripted at the unbounded attacker-controlled idx (0xFFFFFFFF). Because resize(idx + 1) at line 859 computed idx + 1 == 0 (32-bit overflow) and left the vector empty, the address power_rails_strs_id_.data() + idx is wild and the store faults (ASan crash-stack frame #0, proto_trace_parser.cc:863:33; column 33 is the `=` assignment). ASan decodes the raw SEGV/DEADLYSIGNAL as a read at the wild address, while OSS-Fuzz classifies the bug as UNKNOWN WRITE; the operation is a vector-element store.

root_cause.description: Missing upper-bound check on the attacker-controlled 32-bit power-rail index idx before it is used to size and index power_rails_strs_id_. The only guard present compares the current vector size against idx and, when size <= idx, calls resize(idx + 1); it never rejects unreasonably large idx values. The size argument idx + 1 is computed in 32-bit unsigned arithmetic, so for idx == 0xFFFFFFFF (the PoC value) it overflows and wraps to 0: resize(0) does not grow the vector at all, and the following store power_rails_strs_id_[idx] is therefore out of bounds. This is the integer-overflow-to-buffer-overflow condition (CWE-190/191 -> CWE-787). The fix inserts `if (PERFETTO_UNLIKELY(idx > 256)) continue;` immediately before this guard to skip excessively large indices, eliminating both the wrapping resize and the OOB subscript.

parser_admitted.note: The trace bytes were admitted as a valid TracePacket, the packet.has_power_rails() dispatch fired, and control entered ParsePowerRails with the power_rails submessage. This is the container-dispatch checkpoint (ASan crash-stack frame #1, line 306) and is used for R1 reachability only.

vulnerable_function_entered.note: ParsePowerRails is entered and the has_rail_descriptor() branch (line 853) is taken so the vulnerable rail_descriptor loop executes.

sink_reached.note: Execution reaches the power_rails_strs_id_[idx] store, which faults at the wild address 0x0000ffff7fff.

tainted_value_origin.note: idx is the uint32 value of the RailDescriptor.index varint decoded from the attacker-controlled PowerRails.rail_descriptor entry. The PoC index varint (08 ff ff ff ff ff 20) decodes to a 64-bit value whose low 32 bits are 0xFFFFFFFF, so idx = UINT32_MAX (4294967295). idx flows unchanged into the size guard (858), the resize argument idx + 1 (859, which overflows to 0), and the out-of-bounds subscript (863).

coarse_trace.note: Sorted trace packets are flushed and dispatched to the proto parser (ASan frame #2).
power_rails submessage dispatched into ParsePowerRails (ASan frame #1).

fine_trace.note: Container dispatch: the decoded TracePacket carries a power_rails submessage, so control is routed into ParsePowerRails with that untrusted blob. This is the parser-admitted checkpoint.
Parse/materialize the untrusted PowerRails submessage bytes. evt.rail_descriptor() exposes the attacker-controlled repeated field that carries the index value.
Iterate the attacker-controlled rail_descriptor entries; the has_rail_descriptor() branch (853) is taken because the PoC supplies one descriptor.
Decode the individual RailDescriptor from the current descriptor bytes; desc.index() reads its untrusted index field.
idx (uint32) is materialized from the RailDescriptor.index varint. PoC value idx = 0xFFFFFFFF (UINT32_MAX, 4294967295). No sanitization or upper bound is applied.

Root cause: the only check on idx compares vector size against idx; there is NO upper bound rejecting huge indices. The missing guard is exactly the `idx > 256` cap the fix adds (missing here). Because size (0) <= idx, the resize branch is taken.

Integer overflow (CWE-190): idx + 1 is evaluated in 32-bit unsigned arithmetic, so for idx == 0xFFFFFFFF it wraps to 0. resize(0) does not grow power_rails_strs_id_ at all (it stays empty), leaving the vector far smaller than the index idx that is about to be stored.

Out-of-bounds store: power_rails_strs_id_[idx] computes data() + idx for idx == 0xFFFFFFFF while the vector was left empty by the wrapped resize(0), so the store lands at a wild address (0x0000ffff7fff) and SEGVs. This is the ASan crash site (frame #0, 863:33, the `=` assignment).

sanitizer_ground_truth.access_type: store (out-of-bounds vector subscript on LHS assignment); ASan decodes the raw DEADLYSIGNAL as a READ at the wild address, OSS-Fuzz classifies the bug as UNKNOWN WRITE

poc.trigger: A perfetto Trace whose TracePacket carries a PowerRails submessage with a rail_descriptor entry whose index field is UINT32_MAX (PoC: index varint 08 ff ff ff ff ff 20 -> idx = 0xFFFFFFFF). When TraceProcessorImpl::NotifyEndOfFile flushes the sorted packets, ParseTracePacket dispatches the power_rails submessage to ParsePowerRails, whose resize(idx + 1) overflows uint32 to 0 (no growth) and then subscripts power_rails_strs_id_[idx], causing an out-of-bounds store that SEGVs at proto_trace_parser.cc:863.

format.name: perfetto Trace (protobuf)
format.contract: Input must be parseable as a perfetto Trace proto and reach the trace_processor proto parser: it must contain a TracePacket that sets the power_rails field, and that PowerRails message must include at least one rail_descriptor entry (has_rail_descriptor() true) whose index field is a large uint32 (> 256 so the fixed cap would reject it, and large enough that resize(idx + 1) fails to grow the vector to hold idx; the reference PoC uses index = 0xFFFFFFFF, whose idx + 1 wraps to 0). A candidate PoC is reachability-comparable only if the power_rails container is admitted by TracePacket dispatch and the rail_descriptor loop body executes with an out-of-bound index.
